q: How do you keep the statutory certificates up to date, indexed and filed?
a: Inspectors check that every certificate is current and that the file is indexed so any certificate and its survey dates can be produced at once.

q: How do you verify that statutory certificates are authentic, and how often?
a: Cross-check certificate numbers against the class survey status report, and verify electronic certificates on the class/issuer website. Know the company's verification frequency.
t: Master should have access to the class website for e-certificate checks.

q: Does the vessel have any conditions of class or memoranda?
a: A hard-copy class status report was asked for. Memoranda on statutory items are treated as conditions of class. The survey status report should also list CSM items.

q: Your BWTS is not working. What certificate and notifications are needed?
a: Inspectors asked whether a short-term certificate was issued for the BWTS and whether the arrival port and coastal state were told the BWTS was non-functional.

q: What controls are needed before taking SIRE 2.0 photos from height?
a: Photos taken from height (e.g. crane winch limit switch, windlass from the forward mast) need a work-aloft permit, risk assessment and LOTO in place.

q: What makes an acceptable photo for the SIRE 2.0 photo upload?
a: It must show the true current condition, be representative of the area and free of shadows. Use close deck views, show access in the steering gear room view, remove the ETA canvas cover.

q: Is the vessel free from structural defects?
a: Be ready to confirm this with class records, the ESP file and the defect reporting system.

q: How do you prove that drug and alcohol samples were actually collected?
a: Keep the sample receipts for each individual on board so the inspector can verify the samples were really taken.

q: Can all familiarisation items, including reading the SMS manual, be signed on the same day?
a: No. Spread them over the recommended periods (e.g. within 24 hrs, 7 days and 30 days). Everything signed on one date was flagged.

q: Which familiarisation items apply specifically to the ETO?
a: Power generation, electrical and electronic equipment, and all bridge alarms. Inspectors noted there was no dedicated ETO page in the checklist.

q: Which familiarisation items are often missed for catering staff and engineers?
a: Work familiarisation for catering staff, CO2/foam release for everyone, and cargo watch items for engineers (CCR alarms, BWTS start/stop, IG/N2, power pack, VECS).

q: Is mooring familiarisation only for first-time joiners?
a: No. Give it to all mooring crew, especially where equipment differs from the usual set-up (e.g. hydraulic brakes, mooring zone markings).

q: Which visitors need a familiarisation, and what is it checked against?
a: Superintendents, surveyors, vetting inspectors, terminal and cargo reps, bunker suppliers, chandlers. Records must match the gangway log; sailing visitors do both pages.

q: A group boards with the vetting inspector. Who gets the gangway safety briefing?
a: Everyone in the group. A focused briefing given only to the vetting inspector while the others were ignored was flagged.

q: What industry reference should the ECDIS familiarisation checklist include?
a: The Nautical Institute's 'Industry Recommendations for ECDIS Familiarisation'. Its absence was flagged.

q: How often are marine and technical superintendent visit reports expected?
a: Two combined reports within 14 months, no more than 7 months apart (including a 1-month grace period). Office visits at 6-month intervals.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Which activities must be shown as work time in rest-hour records?
a: Drills, manoeuvring, safety and management meetings, cargo start/stop/topping-off, tank cleaning, ODME operation and alarm call-outs.
t: Inspectors compare rest hours with logs, permits and AMS records.

q: The AMS shows an oiler attended an alarm at 0300, but his work hours do not. Why is this a finding?
a: Every call-out recorded in the AMS must also appear in that person's work hours; inspectors cross-check the two.

q: Which records do inspectors compare against rest hours?
a: AMS alarm logs, permit closure times, bunkering times, cargo/tank-cleaning/ODME times, manoeuvring times, meeting records and the shipboard working arrangements.

q: For rest-hour purposes, when does the C/E's work start during bunkering?
a: 30 minutes before the barge comes alongside.

q: During the SSSCL repeat check, whose work hours must also be recorded?
a: The person relieving the CCR duty officer, for the period of relief.

q: Which rest hours are often forgotten for senior deck officers and catering staff?
a: Senior deck officers doing 2nd-level monitoring of cargo operations, and the chief cook/messman receiving provisions in their off-duty time.

q: How many rest-hour non-conformities make a significant finding?
a: Three or more NCs for one person within 30 days is treated as significant and leads to a SIRE observation.

q: How often does the Master review the SMS, and when was the last review?
a: Know the company's required frequency and show the last Master's review record.

q: When was the last internal audit, and how are its findings closed out?
a: Show the internal audit report and the close-out statement for each observation.

q: Is there a procedure for external (third-party) navigation audits?
a: Inspectors asked for the external navigation audit procedure and the third-party audit requirements.

q: What must the office navigation audit report cover?
a: Passage plan, navigation equipment and the Master's self-navigation audit, plus areas for improvement and training needs. Missing these was flagged.

q: What must audit reports show about the auditor?
a: Qualification (Master/C/E) and experience, including tanker types sailed (oil, chemical, LPG) for cargo audits. Applies to navigation, mooring, cargo, engineering and bunker audits.

q: What do inspectors expect for behavioural competency assessments (BCA)?
a: A BCA summary per crew member since joining, showing progress in navigation, cargo, mooring, engineering and bunkering, done by designated assessors with valid training.

q: What engine room simulator training must engineers have?
a: A shore-based ER simulator course within 5 years, per IMO model 1.39/2.07: 21 hrs (3 days) operational level, 40 hrs (5 days) management level. A one-day course was flagged.

q: What should an ER simulator course certificate state?
a: Emergency machinery operation, the ship's propulsion type and the IMO model course duration. Certificates missing these were flagged.

q: When must a Master complete a ship-handling simulator course?
a: When command experience is under 36 months, per STCW Code B-V/a. Model course 1.22 covers BTM/BRM only, not ship handling.

q: Who needs advanced tanker cargo training for the ship type?
a: All officers and the Pumpman should hold advanced training for the tanker type; other ratings may hold basic. Junior officers without advanced oil/chemical endorsement were flagged.
t: Notes differ on junior officers. Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What must the liquid cargo handling simulator (LCHS) course match?
a: The type of vessel being inspected: oil, chemical or gas.

q: Why must the HVPQ be checked thoroughly before an inspection?
a: The compiled VIQ (CVIQ) is generated largely from HVPQ data, so any HVPQ error produces wrong questions in the inspection.

q: From when does the Estimated Index Value (EIV) apply, as asked in HVPQ 1.2.4?
a: From 1 January 2023, for vessels that do not have an EEXI.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What mooring drum details go into the HVPQ?
a: Details of every mooring drum. The SBM mooring line storage drum has a larger diameter than the others.

q: What should the Master's standing orders say about AIS, VHF and passing distances?
a: That AIS/VHF must not be used for collision avoidance, and the safe distance to pass navigational dangers in both open and restricted waters.

q: What should the standing orders say about authority and lines of communication?
a: Set out lines of authority in line with the SMS and explain specific bridge team requirements. An officer unclear about lines of communication was flagged.

q: Must bridge and engine orders be timed?
a: Yes. The orders and each OOW/EOW's reading of them should be timed. Untimed orders were flagged.

q: Is there a procedure for bridge and engine room team composition in different operations?
a: It is expected: watch composition for drifting, underway, storing and personnel transfer, considering traffic, hazards, weather and visibility.

q: What do inspectors check about the last port State control inspection?
a: The last PSC report and evidence that all deficiencies are closed out.

q: What happens if the ship gets a CII 'D' rating three years in a row?
a: The notes describe D as 'satisfactory' and say the final CII phase began in January 2025. Know your attained CII and the follow-up actions required.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: By when must class issue the Statement of Compliance for the previous year?
a: Before 31 May of the following year (the notes link this to EEXI/EEDI). EEDI is mandatory for ships built after 1 January 2013.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: The P&I certificate says persistent oil will not be carried, but the ship carries it. What is required?
a: Managers must notify the club. Not reporting earlier persistent-oil voyages was flagged.

q: What makes a power-failure drill unacceptable?
a: Table-top only, unrealistic drills that do not genuinely test the shipboard emergency plans were flagged.

q: What else is expected in drill records and procedures?
a: Lessons learnt in each record, all required drills done (a missed mast riser fire drill was flagged) and a company procedure on safety during drills.

q: Give examples of drills SIRE 2.0 expects under ISM 8.1.
a: Emergency towing, hazardous cargo reaction/vapour/gas release, hull failure, excessive list, ME and power failure, collision, grounding, flooding, heavy weather, serious injury, helicopter medevac.

q: Which regulations require drills for steering failure, recovery from water, piracy, and oil/NLS spills?
a: SOLAS V/26; SOLAS III/17-1; ISPS Code A/13.4; MARPOL Annex I reg 37 and Annex II reg 17.

q: When should AIS be switched off?
a: When alongside a terminal or in a port area where hydrocarbon gases may be present.

q: How quickly must a defect be raised in the defect reporting system?
a: Within 48 hours.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What handover period is required at crew change, and what is it checked against?
a: A 12-hour handover/takeover. Inspectors compared it with gangway log times and found a mismatch.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Must ballast tank repairs done in dry dock be recorded as defects?
a: Yes. Repairs shown in the executive hull summary but missing from the defect records were flagged.

q: What is needed for personnel transfer by basket?
a: A contingency plan for basket transfers, and training certificates that specifically say 'personnel transfer'.

q: How long is a CAP rating valid?
a: It has no expiry date; it reflects the ship's condition on the inspection date. Each charterer sets its own validity period.

q: Must the officers' matrix be available, and who can be left out?
a: Yes, it must be available. New joiners from the last 4 days need not be included.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Do you have a certificate for the spare magnetic compass?
a: Inspectors asked for it, so keep the spare compass certificate available.

q: How many post-incident urine sample kits are needed, and who holds them?
a: Enough for the whole complement, including the Master, kept in the Master's possession.

q: How many blows can an alcometer take before it must be replaced?
a: Normally 200-300. Press and hold the power button to see how many have been used.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Is management of change (MOC) needed for a like-for-like replacement?
a: Be ready to show the procedure that states MOC is not required for like-for-like.

q: Does the SMS cover spaces that are not classed as enclosed spaces?
a: Inspectors asked to see the procedure covering such spaces.

q: How often is the personnel transfer basket proof-load tested?
a: Every 2 years, to twice the designated weight.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: From when must the pilot ladder be listed in Form E?
a: From 1 January 2026 (item 3.1.16).

q: Which IMO resolution requires CO2 measurement before enclosed space entry?
a: MSC.581(110), effective 3 December 2025. Inspectors asked for the company procedure and the enclosed space register.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What are the company's risk assessment requirements?
a: Be ready to show the list of tasks/scenarios for which a risk assessment is required.

q: What do inspectors look for in permit-to-work records?
a: Hot work, enclosed space and work aloft permits fully completed. Repeat gas readings must be recorded, and the person approving an enclosed space permit must not enter the space.

q: The entry permit sets benzene and H2S evacuation at 50% of 1 ppm. How will you measure that?
a: Inspectors expect you to show equipment that can actually detect that low level (0.5 ppm), as the permit demands.

q: Where is the onboard crew complaints procedure?
a: Know the procedure and show where it is posted and filed.

q: What should the Garbage Management Plan look like?
a: Vessel-specific (not a generic fleet file), reviewed, read by all crew with a record, and include company measures to reduce garbage.

q: What is checked for IGS operation and PV valve testing?
a: IGS operation, PV valve test records and the type approval certificate of the PV valve test kit.

q: Which lists should be decided on the basis of a risk assessment?
a: The list of enclosed spaces, the mooring zone marking and the list of critical spares.

q: Which edition of COSWP should be on board?
a: The notes call for the new 2026 edition.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What is the maximum weight of a heaving line monkey fist?
a: Not more than 500 g (COSWP section 26.3.6).

q: What is required for entry into the N2 generator room?
a: An entry procedure and an O2 meter at both entrances (a CDI requirement). Atmosphere results and entry/exit times should be recorded.

q: When must the fixed O2 analyser be calibrated before starting the IG/N2 system?
a: Within 24 hours before starting the system.

q: What security items are checked at the gangway?
a: That the current security level is applied, plus the inventory and maintenance records of security and ship-hardening equipment.

q: What cyber security evidence will the inspector ask for?
a: Shore cyber training, IT/OT register, access and admin procedures, backups, USB checks, updated antivirus, cyber RA, contingency plan, IT contact, locked IT/OT spaces, awareness, policy.

q: How does the new COSWP define working at height (aloft)?
a: Anyone working where there is a risk of falling may be regarded as working at height (COSWP 17.1.1).

q: You hear the emergency alarm at 0200. What do you do?
a: Go to your muster station. That is the answer the inspector wanted to hear from crew.

q: Is there a procedure for using a double (criss-cross) rope stopper?
a: One is expected; its absence was flagged.

q: How should the vapour manifold be marked and fitted?
a: Two 10 cm red bands with 'VAPOUR' stencil; cruciform bollard (600 mm high), pad eye (SWL 15 t) and Panama lead in line; threaded stud bolt (1/2 inch dia, 1 inch protruding).

q: Could you start the emergency generator if asked?
a: Inspectors asked deck officers, the Pumpman and the Bosun to start it, so deck staff must know how.

q: How is a portable gas meter calibrated and bump-tested, and how are its alarms set?
a: An engineer was asked to explain calibration, alarm and pre-alarm settings, and how to carry out a bump test. All officers should know this.

q: Your multi-gas meter hose is 15 m but the tank is 20 m deep. Can you still sample?
a: Per the GX-6000 maker, yes: increase the sampling time to 90 seconds or more and a 20 m hose can be used.

q: Why might a multi-gas meter show zero O2 in a crude oil tank?
a: Toxic vapours can stop the O2 sensor (stated in the maker's manual). Avoid sampling direct under pressure or with moisture; collect the gas in a sample bag first.

q: What is expected for deck-mounted cargo heaters?
a: Testing and operation records, and the company testing requirement for periods when heating is not used.

q: Are cargo tank isolating valves maintained and tested?
a: Each isolating valve should be maintained and tested. Missing records were flagged.

q: What hearing protection is needed when passing the ER blowers on rounds?
a: Ear muffs.

q: Which deck condition defects are commonly flagged?
a: Painted hatch cover cleat washers, windlass brake spindle at its last thread, illegible BRC marks on drums, plastic-sheathed mast stays, unreadable draft/Plimsoll marks.

q: How do you test the loadicator, and what variation is allowed?
a: Run test conditions and compare the results; the notes allow 2-5% variation.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What is the purpose of the VRCS accumulator?
a: To prevent pressure surges in the valve remote control system.

q: What is the rule of thumb for cargo valve opening time?
a: About 2 seconds per inch of valve size. Compare recorded times with the yard's figures.

q: What is the worst-case damage stability condition for the present loading?
a: Know the worst case and how it is identified; the notes say to consider the five load line rules. The Master should also know it.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What are the requirements for portable cargo hold lights?
a: Non-conductive shades and supply voltage not above 50 V (COSWP 18.15.2). 220 V lamps were flagged.

q: Can you upload a photo taken on a sister ship?
a: No. A photo from another vessel was flagged because it did not show the double block and bleed valve fitted on board.

q: What records are needed for double block and bleed (DBB) valves?
a: Maintenance records and proof of automatic operation, including the DBB valve on the N2 line.

q: Should the chain locker be marked as an enclosed space?
a: Yes. An unmarked chain locker missed in the safety inspection was flagged.

q: Is there a procedure for inerting tanks before loading?
a: One is expected; its absence was flagged.

q: When must ballast tank repairs be added to the Coating Technical File?
a: After any repair or recoating of a ballast tank. A C/O unaware of this and missing repair records were flagged.

q: Which ships need a Coating Technical File under SOLAS II-1/3-2?
a: Contract on/after 1 July 2008, or keel laid on/after 1 Jan 2009 if no contract, or delivery on/after 1 July 2012. On crude tankers it covers ballast tanks, voids and cargo tanks.

q: What lifebuoy faults are commonly found?
a: Buoyant line tied up and not ready for use, and the lifebuoy light attached to the lifeline instead of the buoy body.

q: Where must liferaft launching instructions be posted?
a: Under the emergency lighting. A C/O doing monthly inspections who was unaware of this was flagged.

q: What must the machinery space safety inspection cover?
a: Vessel-specific hot surfaces and flammable liquids, using the ship-specific checklist.

q: What securing issues are often missed in monthly safety inspections?
a: Unsecured steel pipes, tank cleaning machines, reducers and washing machines (e.g. in the N2 room). Items must be secured and the findings recorded.

q: What record is needed before mooring winch brake testing?
a: A record that the hydraulic jack was calibrated before the test.

q: On which layer is the brake test done when the drum is not split?
a: On the outermost (top) layer.

q: At what load should the winch brake render, and what goes into the calculation?
a: 60% of SDMBL. Inputs: jack pressure (P), piston area (A), lever from drum centre to jack point (L), drum diameter (Dd, not winch) and rope diameter (Dr).

q: What is checked on winch brakes of drums in active mooring service?
a: That each brake is correctly tightened. An incorrectly tightened brake on a working drum was flagged.

q: What surface should warping drums have?
a: A non-skid surface. Painted drums were flagged (COSWP 26.8.3).

q: What should the gangway's last step (platform) be marked with?
a: The load from the gangway maker's plate; the platform is not designed for the full number of persons often marked. A means to measure the maximum angle is also needed.

q: What are the angle limits for the gangway, MOT ladder and pilot combination arrangement?
a: Gangway 0-55 deg; MOT ladder normally max 30 deg unless designed otherwise; combination arrangement for pilots 0-45 deg, with deck pad eye for 48 kN.

q: At what IG pressure do cargo pumps usually trip on IG failure?
a: Often at 100 mmWG.

q: Who should sign the cargo plan?
a: In addition to deck staff, all engineers and the terminal representative should sign the last page.

q: Why is ticking an SSSCL item you do not understand a risk?
a: An officer ticked the insulating flange item in the repeat check but knew nothing about it. Inspectors test the knowledge behind every tick.

q: How is the 0400 SSSCL repeat check done when watchkeepers work 6 on/6 off?
a: Someone relieves the duty officer so he can make the round of the ship.

q: What error is allowed in the brake test pressure gauge?
a: +/- 2-3% per OCIMF and class guidelines. Know the company procedure.

q: How is oily water from forecastle store or BT room bilges handled?
a: Show an expanded procedure for monitoring these bilges and for disposal, not just the words 'dispose safely'.

q: Which safety items are often missed during safety rounds?
a: Water inside the forward liferaft light, a rescue harness blocked by closed grating, no non-skid on forecastle/poop, faded IMO symbols.

q: How detailed should the cargo plan be?
a: Specific: which tanks, cargo and ballast pumps to start, and what the C/O expects of each officer and crew member, not general statements.

q: Which critical stages should a cargo plan identify?
a: Arm connection/disconnection, gangway/MOT rigging, ullaging/sampling, start, stop, topping off, stripping, COW, grade change, IG/N2 failure, start of ballasting.

q: A checklist said 'yes' for portable COW drives that no longer exist. What is the lesson?
a: Checklist answers must reflect the equipment actually on board.

q: What is expected of the forward emergency towing arrangement?
a: No extra lashings that would prevent quick deployment.

q: Where must face shields be available?
a: In the chemical locker and wherever chemicals are used: paint room, battery room, sample locker, along with chemical gloves, apron and goggles.

q: Where should inertia-reel fall arrestors be made mandatory?
a: In the PPE matrix and work aloft checklist. Not making them obligatory was flagged.

q: Is a smoking policy required?
a: Yes. It must exist and be implemented; a missing policy was flagged.

q: Is the accommodation ladder turntable and pin included in the PMS?
a: It should be. Leaving its inspection and maintenance out of the PMS was flagged.

q: How do you prevent misuse of the ODME sampling line?
a: Fit an environmental seal on the ferrule joint at the processing box so a fresh water line cannot be connected.

q: What is checked for personnel transfer by crane?
a: The approval certificate of the personnel transfer basket and training records for crane personnel transfer.

q: IG pressure sensors activate but the PV valve does not lift. Two possible reasons?
a: Palm oil solidifying in cold climates, and polymerising cargo sticking in the PV valve.

q: How is testing of forepeak store bilges evidenced?
a: By deck log book entries for the bilge tests.

q: How do you know the fixed foam is suitable for the cargo carried?
a: IBC Code chapter 17, column L, gives the fire-fighting media for each cargo.

q: How do you know the foam mixer is set correctly?
a: The foam analysis report shows the concentrate type (1%, 3% or 6%); the mixer must be set to that value.

q: By when must PFOS-containing firefighting foam be removed?
a: SOLAS II-2/10, as amended by MSC.532(107), bans PFOS foam from 1 January 2026.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: How should personal gas meter and fixed gas detection alarms be set?
a: To company TLV values for HC and H2S. Incorrect warning/alarm settings were flagged; know how to set fixed system alarms.

q: Explain TLV-TWA, TLV-STEL and TLV-C.
a: TWA: 8 hrs a day, 5 days a week. STEL: 15 minutes, up to 4 times a day, at least 60 minutes apart. Ceiling: never to be exceeded, not even for a second.

q: What rule of thumb estimates vapour concentration from vapour pressure?
a: Concentration (ppm) is roughly vapour pressure (mmHg) x 1300.

q: What is expected for the fixed gas detection cabinet and bridge remote unit?
a: The cabinet should be sealable and kept closed, not opened often. Testing of the bridge remote unit must be recorded.

q: What format must MSDS/SDS follow?
a: Annex I cargoes and oil fuel: MSC.286(86). Annex II cargoes: GHS format per MSC/Circ.1100 and/or MEPC/Circ.407.

q: What is IPTA?
a: The International Parcel Tankers Association - for chemical tankers, similar to INTERTANKO.

q: How often is the accommodation ladder inspected, and its falls renewed?
a: Inspected 5-yearly with falls renewed within 5 years; the company in the notes required wire renewal every 24 months.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What is the 'target operating pressure' in the VOC manual?
a: A pre-set tank pressure based on cargo, ambient conditions and equipment, kept on passage to cut VOC emissions and needless venting. Varies with cargo SVP (MEPC.1/Circ.680).

q: When is a gangway safety net needed?
a: Deployed at gangways as per ISGOTT 16.4.3.4.

q: How do you know a cargo is suitable for COW, and who may do COW?
a: Check cargo viscosity against the COW manual. The company procedure defines the officer qualification for COW.

q: How can you load crude denser than seawater (1.025)?
a: Only with calculations (tank load density, sloshing) carried out by the yard/class.

q: Can an EEBD use a filter-type respirator?
a: No.

q: What IBC Code safety equipment sets are required?
a: At least 3 sets beyond SOLAS II-2/10.10, suitable for all COF cargoes and flammable atmospheres, with SCBA (no stored oxygen), ready to don, and a charged spare cylinder of 6000 L or more.
t: A crew member trained by the maker to service the SCBA was also asked for.

q: What evidence is needed for chemical protective suits and eye protection?
a: A chemical resistance list for the suits and proof they suit flammable atmospheres. Chemical goggles, not safety spectacles, in chemical environments.

q: Can synthetic ropes be used to lower items into tanks?
a: No.

q: Static accumulator cargo into a non-inerted tank: what initial loading rate applies?
a: Max 1 m/s at the tank inlet for 30 min or until twice the shore line content has loaded (whichever is less), incl. filling to twice the inlet pipe diameter.

q: Which practices are not allowed with static accumulator cargo in non-inerted tanks?
a: Over-the-top or splash filling, bulk rate over 1 m/s when the cargo is not 'clean', and blowing lines with compressed air after loading.

q: Loading a low-volatility static accumulator into an uncleaned non-inerted tank that held a high-volatility cargo: what is needed?
a: Full static electricity precautions. Skipping them in this case was flagged.

q: What ballast tank filling rate is used for calculation purposes?
a: The notes give 36 m/s.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What VECS records and knowledge are checked?
a: Operation and testing, O2 meter calibration, inspections, operator training, the VECS diagram, pressure settings, initial and max flow rates.

q: Tank cleaning after a volatile product in a non-inert tank: key rules?
a: No free fall, no steam, bond sounding rods/UTI before insertion. Do not start washing above 10% LFL and stop if it exceeds 35% LFL.

q: What is a volatile product?
a: Petroleum with a closed-cup flash point below 60 C, or handled within 10 C of its flash point (e.g. flash point 80 C handled at 70 C or above).

q: What is checked on deepwell pump cofferdams?
a: Leak monitoring, purge medium compatible with recent cargoes, water filling for corrosives, and a defect report when leakage exceeds maker limits or a pump is blocked.

q: What rules apply to manifold reducers and spool pieces?
a: Faces protected in stowage; marked with test pressure and the same MAWP as the connection; only one spool piece; long spools supported.

q: What manifold precautions apply on a chemical tanker?
a: Spray guards on flanges for acids/toxic/corrosive cargoes, edge protection and warnings on raised platforms, and no mixing of incompatible cargoes in drip trays/drain tanks.

q: What is the lowest working temperature of the PV breaker fluid?
a: It depends on the glycol mix: 20% gives -8 C, 40% -25 C, 60% -50 C, 80% -45 C, 100% -12 C.

q: What is done with the cargo heating system when carrying non-heated cargo?
a: Isolate the heating for non-heated cargoes and check the observation tank for any leakage.

q: Where is the procedure for using the overfill alarm in navigation mode at sea?
a: Inspectors asked for the procedure covering use of the cargo overfill alarm system while at sea.

q: What must be reviewed before a contractor's cargo doping (additive) operation?
a: The doping plan, MSDS, no free fall of additive into a non-inert tank, toxicity, flammability, PPE, clean-up contingency and an RA for the whole operation.

q: How do you test and calibrate a PT100 cargo temperature sensor?
a: Connect a Fluke meter at the junction box, read the resistance and convert it to temperature using the table.

q: How should loading arm and manifold loads be supported?
a: Never on empty oil drums. Drip tray grating load density 1 t/m2; spread tripod loads with wooden planks.

q: What is the service rating of your UTI, and what if fixed gauging fails?
a: Know whether the UTI is rated 'restricted' or 'closed', and the company procedure for fixed gauging failure.

q: How often is the fixed cargo temperature monitoring system calibrated?
a: Every 30 months, per the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Which category Y cargoes need a prewash?
a: Highly viscous or solidifying cargoes, or when the stripping system has failed.

q: What must the P&A manual state about stripping?
a: The stripping time.

q: What is a tripartite agreement for chemical cargo?
a: Per the notes: seller, buyer and flag agree carriage of a cargo not listed in the COF. Details go to IMO for the MEPC.2/Circular within 30 days.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Where do you find information on chemical cargoes not listed in the COF?
a: The MEPC.2/Circular, maintained by IMO and updated annually.

q: What must be in place for inhibited cargoes?
a: A procedure, valid inhibitor certificate, RA, care with anti-freeze, exclusion of water, inhibitor toxicity info and a contingency for uncontrolled polymerisation.

q: Why must a cargo with an oxygen-dependent inhibitor not be inerted?
a: The inhibitor needs a minimum oxygen level. Inerting, clearing lines with N2, or not monitoring vapour-space O2 were all flagged.

q: Vinyl chloride carried without enough inhibitor: what O2 limit applies to the IG?
a: Oxygen in the inert gas must be below 0.1% by volume.

q: Tanks with vapour isolating valves closed for segregation: what venting is required?
a: Either two full-flow PV valves, or a PV valve plus a pressure/vacuum monitoring system, on the tank side of the isolating valve.

q: What are the minimum functions of a linked ship/shore ESD?
a: Either side can trip the other, auto-trip on power loss or damage, 5-pin twist connectors, audible/visual alarm, health and reset indication, testable at sea and in port.

q: What ESD knowledge do inspectors test?
a: Valve closing times, when ESD may be inhibited (maintenance, dry-docking, testing, special operations), and the testing procedure and records.

q: Name some optional ESD activators.
a: Fire detection, tank overfill, loss of valve control pressure, excessive transfer pressure, critical valve movement, surge drum high level, MLA limits, MLA PERC activation.

q: Where should the emergency cargo pump be stored?
a: In a dry atmosphere.

q: What is expected for leaking tank hatch covers?
a: Leak testing of the hatch covers and a risk assessment for any leaking cover.

q: What is needed to use an electronic Oil Record Book?
a: Written confirmation from flag/RO, automatic backup to offline storage, and a data recovery method if the system fails.

q: Oily sludge or bilge water is moved into cargo slop tanks. What must be recorded?
a: A matching (reciprocal) entry in ORB Part II as well.

q: Where do you record exceptional uptake of ballast water into cargo tanks?
a: In the Ballast Water Record Book and in ORB Part II / Cargo Record Book. The BWMP must be flag-approved.

q: What distance and depth apply to ballast water exchange (D-1)?
a: 200 nm from land in 200 m depth; at minimum 50 nm from shore.

q: Why would equal departure and arrival drafts after a long passage raise questions?
a: Ballast taken on passage must be recorded in the BWRB. Here it was missing.

q: What must you do about defects that affect SSSCL items?
a: Bring them to the attention of the terminal representative.

q: What should cargo/port planning documents say about supervision?
a: The level of supervision and support needed at each stage of the cargo/port operation.

q: What loading computer records are expected?
a: Accuracy verification at special survey with a class surveyor, and lightship updated after weight changes such as BWTS or EGCS installation.

q: What cargo hose checks are expected?
a: Stowed above min bend radius; continuity (max 6 ohm/m) and elongation tests; rated at least 10.2 kg/cm2; compatible with cargo and temperature; within design flow rate.

q: What must the Mooring System Management Plan show about line angles?
a: The maximum permitted horizontal deviation from perpendicular to the ship's fore-aft axis, and the vertical line angles.

q: What manoeuvring readiness does SSSCL point 32 (part 6) refer to?
a: Tanker manoeuvring readiness, i.e. 'short notice' as per TSG para 2.11.

q: What mooring analysis is needed when double-banked?
a: An analysis showing the mooring plan restrains both the inside and outside ships.

q: What terminal information should be on board?
a: The terminal booklet and mooring plan (with evidence of the Master/agent's effort to get it), and records that junior officers read it.

q: Which STS items do inspectors check?
a: Use of the vapour balancing checklist, the other ship's previous cargo (esp. high H2S) in the STS checklist, and JPO measures against arcing between ships.

q: What procedure is needed for a vapour return system manifold (VRSM) at single buoy moorings?
a: A specific procedure for the VRSM; its absence was flagged.

q: What lighting level is required at the cargo manifold?
a: 100 lux.

q: What minimum capacity is noted for the small oil/chemical spill container?
a: 2 m3, per the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Washings after an Annex I cargo were discharged using Annex II criteria. What went wrong?
a: The officer did not realise the previous cargo was Annex I. Know each cargo's annex before applying discharge criteria.

q: Which mooring set-up errors are flagged?
a: Synthetic ropes on drums designed for wires, the fire wire recovery motor left in place while fire wires were in use, and chafed mooring ropes.

q: What is required of anti-piracy bullet-proof shutters?
a: They must be fully transparent.

q: Can a fire station door be kept locked?
a: No. A locked fire station door was flagged.

q: What winterisation measures are expected?
a: Mast riser drain min 50 mm, covers on valves/pumps/vents/PV valves, record crack-opened valves, remove water from gearboxes, use winter checklists, run ballast heating.

q: What is a 'dead-leg' and why does it matter in sub-zero conditions?
a: A section of piping that rarely or never sees flow. Minimising dead-legs helps pumps work in sub-zero conditions.

q: How should cargo samples be stored?
a: As per the segregation table.

q: How must heated and heat-sensitive cargoes be separated?
a: These notes say one complete tank; recent CDI notes say two complete compartments.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What is required before entering ballast tanks on a ship with electrolysis BWTS?
a: Chlorine tests before entry, and crew trained on the vessel-specific BWTS.

q: How should paint drums and the paint store be kept?
a: Drums secured, especially on upper racks, with apron and gloves available in the paint locker.

q: What is the MSMPR?
a: The Mooring System Management Plan (MSMP) register.

q: Which guidelines apply to towing and mooring equipment?
a: MEG3/MEG4; MSC.1/Circ.1175 for ships of 1 Jan 2007 to 1 Jan 2024, and MSC.1/Circ.1175/Rev.1 after 1 Jan 2024.

q: When must a wire rope be discarded?
a: With 4 broken wires in 6d or 8 broken wires in 30d.

q: How many turns should stay on the split drum?
a: Generally 5-6 for synthetic ropes and 10 for wire, but this varies by maker.

q: What SWL should shore bollards have for one, two, three and four hooks?
a: 100%, 120%, 180% and 240% of SDMBL respectively.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What strength should mooring tails have?
a: Tail design break force (TDBF) of 125-130% of SDMBL.

q: What is the minimum D/d bend ratio for ropes?
a: Minimum 15 (D = roller diameter, d = rope diameter).

q: What is the SWL of the rope stopper staple (eye)?
a: 50% of SDMBL.

q: What surface must the pilot boarding point on deck have?
a: An anti-skid surface.

q: Bow chain stoppers on ships built from 2009: how many and what SWL?
a: Up to 100,000 dwt: 1 x 200 t; 100-150,000 dwt: 1 x 250 t; over 150,000 dwt: 2 x 350 t. Fairlead 2.7-3.7 m ahead of stopper, pedestal roller 3 m behind.

q: Bow chain stoppers on ships built before 2009: how many and what SWL?
What are the main types of fibre mooring rope?
a: Polyester, polypropylene, polyethylene, blends and polyamide (nylon), which loses about 15% strength when wet.

q: What is the working load limit (WLL) of synthetic and wire ropes?
a: Synthetic 50% of SDMBL; wire 55% of SDMBL.

q: What are the helicopter landing area ('H') zone markings?
a: Clear zone D with 0.3 m yellow line; touchdown circle 0.5D with white H (4 x 3 m) on dark green; manoeuvring zone 2D. No obstructions over 25 cm.

q: What are the helicopter 'winch only' area markings?
a: Clear zone min 5 m dia in yellow; inner circle 1.5D white line, no obstruction over 3 m, 'WINCH ONLY'; outer circle 2D dotted yellow, nothing over 6 m.

q: What emergency equipment must be ready for helicopter operations?
a: Red signal lamp (IS on tanker deck), axe, crowbar, wrench, fire blanket, 60 cm cutters, insulated hook, hacksaw + 6 blades, ladder, 5 mm x 15 m lifeline, pliers, screwdrivers, knife, first aid kit.

q: If HVPQ 5.2.1.1 (helicopter operations) is answered 'yes', what must be in place?
a: Helicopter RA, training/drill requirements, landing area plan, ICS helicopter checklist, assigned officer and crew, emergency equipment, limits on cargo/crane work.

q: How must emergency escape routes be marked?
a: With IMO signs and photoluminescent 'emergency escape route' notices and direction signs in accommodation, machinery spaces, pump rooms and similar spaces.

q: When may tank high-level alarms be isolated?
a: Only during maintenance, dry-docking or repairs. Know where the company manual covers failure of fixed gauging and high-level alarms.

q: What conductivity defines a static accumulator oil?
a: Below 50 pS/m (can hold a significant charge). Above 50 pS/m is a non-accumulator.

q: What should the risk assessment for a hydro blaster say?
a: That it must not be used during tank cleaning, gas freeing or purging.

q: How is a cargo pump's MAWP estimated from its head?
a: From the liquid column: 1 m of seawater is about 0.1 bar (P = d.g.h). A pump rated 130 mLC is roughly 13 bar.

q: What test pressure is used for cargo line pressure testing?
a: The notes say 'more than 15 times the MAWP' - probably meant 1.5 times.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Is there a distraction policy for cargo operations?
a: There should be: similar to the bridge distraction policy and posted in the CCR.

q: When should an ECDIS route check be done, and where is it logged?
a: Know when the company requires a route check and record it in the ECDIS/ENC log the company specifies.

q: On some ECDIS models the route check shows every hazard at the start of the leg. What does this mean?
a: On that model (e.g. Furuno) hazards and UKC limits are flagged at the beginning of the leg, not at the exact spot, so you must check the whole leg yourself.

q: Which bridge equipment performance tests are commonly asked for?
a: NAVTEX, echo sounder and AIS performance tests.

q: When are bridge team meetings held, and where are they recorded?
a: Know when the company requires them and where they are logged. Briefings and debriefings must be specific, not generic.

q: What is the company safety depth/contour policy, and will you get more alarms after crossing the safety contour?
a: Know the company policy and be ready to explain what alarms (if any) follow after the safety contour is crossed.

q: When should the ECDIS hard drive be replaced?
a: As per the maker's recommendation, often every 2 years.

q: What must the safety depth calculation include?
a: CATZOC allowance (+) and height of tide (-), the same as the UKC calculation (NP232 para 12.12). Leaving them out was flagged.

q: What error is allowed in the speed log?
a: 2% of the ship's speed or 0.2 kn, whichever is greater.

q: How does accuracy testing differ for EM and Doppler logs?
a: EM logs give STW only; Doppler logs give STW and SOG (dual-axis adds athwartship speed). Comparing EM STW with GPS SOG is not valid, as current is unknown.

q: Which bridge team management publication should be on board?
a: The Bridge Team Management book was republished in 2024. The company in the notes supplied BRM vol 1 and 2 instead.

q: Which COLREG rule was the OOW asked about?
a: Rule 19 - conduct of vessels in restricted visibility.

q: What lights does a NUC vessel making way show (Rule 27(a)(iii))?
a: Its NUC lights plus sidelights and a sternlight. A bridge poster missing the sternlight was flagged at a CDI.

q: What sound signal does a vessel aground make in restricted visibility?
a: The bell signal with three separate and distinct strokes before and after the rapid ringing of the bell forward.

q: Does COLREGs define 'underway but stopped', and is a drifting ship underway?
a: There is no such definition. 'Underway' excludes anchored, moored or aground vessels but not drifting ones.

q: What is the range and position of the Morse signalling light?
a: Range 5 nm; about 2 m above or below the main mast light, and at least 2 m above the forward mast.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What is the audibility range of the whistle (fog signal)?
a: 2 nm for ships over 200 m; 1.5 nm for ships under 200 m.

q: What is the luminous intensity of masthead, side and stern lights?
a: Masthead 6 nm (about 92 candela); sidelights and sternlight 3 nm (12 candela).
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What are the horizontal and vertical sector limits of navigation lights?
a: Horizontal cut-off: sidelights 1-3 deg, masthead/stern 5 deg. Vertical: 5 deg above and below.
t: Source wrote '1/3 deg'. Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What sound level is a gong in the after part of the ship?
a: 110 dB at 1 m distance.

q: When are bow crossing range (BCR) and CPA both zero?
a: Per the notes: head-on on a collision course, or with zero relative speed to the other vessel.

q: Why should BNWAS not be left in 'auto' mode?
a: Per MSC.128(75), auto mode activates BNWAS only when autopilot/track control is in use; it is inhibited the rest of the time.

q: Which BNWAS tests are expected before departure?
a: 2nd and 3rd stage alarms, dormant period, and emergency power - stages 1-3 tested on both main and secondary power, with records.

q: What is the BNWAS dormant period, and how do the alarm stages follow?
a: Dormant period 3-12 min. Then 15 s to 2nd stage, then 90 s to 3rd stage (up to 3 min on large ships). Stages 2 and 3 may be combined except on passenger ships.

q: What timing accuracy is required for BNWAS, and who may change its mode?
a: 5% or 5 s, whichever is less. Mode and dormant period controls should be security protected, Master only.

q: What is rudder creeping?
a: The rudder drifting off midships when one steering motor is running and the rudder was set midships.

q: What does 'Fl(3) G 5s 12M' mean on a chart?
a: Group flashing 3, green, period 5 seconds, nominal range 12 nm.

q: How can you estimate the drift of a disabled ship?
a: Use section 3.4.3 of 'Peril at Sea and Salvage'.

q: What is a trial manoeuvre?
a: Inspectors asked officers to explain and demonstrate the ARPA trial manoeuvre function.

q: What is a limiting danger line (LDL)?
a: The marking of the no-go area.

q: What was your UKC when passing over a pipeline marked on the ECDIS?
a: Inspectors expect you to know it and show it in the passage plan.

q: What do you do if the steering gear hydraulic lock alarm activates?
a: Switch to the standby steering system and have engineers find the root cause.

q: If both GPS feeds to ECDIS fail, does DR mode start automatically?
a: Yes, automatically.

q: When must the X-band radar magnetron be replaced?
a: As per the maker's interval, shown in the PMS. Know the company procedure if it cannot be replaced on time.

q: When was the magnetic compass last adjusted?
a: Show the adjustment record and the swing circle from the course recorder.

q: A compass error by the moon was logged on a new-moon night. Why is that a finding?
a: The moon was not visible then, so the record could not be genuine.

q: What is a GNSS compass, and when is it required?
a: A non-magnetic heading device that can replace a gyro for AIS, radar and ARPA heading. Required in polar waters above 80 deg latitude.

q: What mistake is often made when printing tides from tidal software?
a: Not applying the zone time, so the tide is not in local time.

q: How often is VDR data downloaded?
a: Quarterly, per the company in the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: How often are radar performance and the GPS feed into ECDIS checked?
a: Per the company in the notes: radar performance at the end of each watch, GPS feed to ECDIS every watch.

q: Can the LRIT Sat-C and SSAS Sat-C be used interchangeably?
a: No.

q: How is Sea Area A3 now defined?
a: An area outside A1 and A2 within coverage of a recognised mobile satellite service (Inmarsat or Iridium) supported by the ship's SES, with continuous alerting.

q: Is NBDP still part of GMDSS equipment?
a: No. NBDP is now redundant and no longer part of GMDSS equipment.

q: What rules apply to portable two-way radios?
a: Keep them on trickle charge at all times, do not test on Ch 16, and know the limits on using non-IS radios outside the bridge.

q: What is the difference between solid-state and magnetron radars?
a: Inspectors ask officers to explain this difference for the radars on board.

q: What is the difference between a distress alert and a distress message?
a: Hold the distress button about 4 s to send the alert; holding longer may bring up a list to choose the nature of distress.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Can you simulate the 5 mandatory ECDIS alarms?
a: Inspectors asked officers to demonstrate the simulation of the 5 mandatory alarms.

q: How is the echo sounder tested?
a: Test the depth alarm at different ranges and follow the company procedure on what checks are done and when.

q: How do you verify position accuracy on the ECDIS?
a: By radar overlay and visual fixes.

q: What are the 2-shade and 4-shade depth displays, and when are they used?
a: Know both modes and what the company says about them; the notes link their use to night time.

q: What VDR condition defects are commonly flagged?
a: A painted VDR capsule and faded or missing reflective strips.

q: What do you check on the VDR after a bridge equipment repair?
a: Do a performance test and make sure the repaired equipment's feed is still reaching the VDR.

q: How do you check whether the ECDIS display is at compilation scale?
a: Inspectors ask you to show this on the ECDIS.

q: Which documents are checked for a pilotage passage?
a: Passage plan, pilot card, Master-pilot exchange checklist, and pre-arrival and pre-departure checklists (which confirm the bridge equipment checks).

q: How should the pilot be integrated into the bridge team?
a: Brief the pilot, record EPL status on the pilot card, keep the Master in command, give the pilot one ECDIS and one radar, and mark the mooring sequence.

q: What must be logged if the EPL seal is removed or the limit overridden?
a: A log book entry, e.g. when the EPL is removed for an Australian port.

q: Where must transfer of the con between Master and pilot be recorded?
a: In the bell book or pilot card. Missing records were flagged.

q: What records of celestial navigation are expected?
a: Sextant sights with position lines plotted and compared with the GPS position.

q: Which weather fax and NAVTEX stations are you using?
a: Be ready to show proof of the stations in use.

q: The duty engineer calls to say he is going into the UMS engine room. What do you do?
a: Monitor him: he should call the bridge and switch on the dead-man alarm before entry, and report when he leaves.

q: What is the ECDIS safety cone/frame setting, and what is it now?
a: Know what the setting does and be able to show the current value.

q: How do you check ECDIS safety settings at each stage of the passage?
a: Calculate safety settings (safety contour/depth, look-ahead, alarms) for each leg. Not doing this for each leg was flagged.

q: How do you check the expiry of VDR reserve power and beacon batteries?
a: Check the expiry dates of the VDR reserve power battery and the acoustic beacon battery.

q: Why have both X-band and S-band radars?
a: Inspectors ask for the advantages and disadvantages of each and which to use in restricted visibility and rain.

q: How do you show that security chart Q6099 is corrected?
a: Show the latest correction (the inspector asked for a 2024 one) and its record in the chart correction log.

q: Is the pilot part of the bridge team, and what bridge watch level applies?
a: Know the watch level composition for pilotage. The pilot should be integrated into the bridge team.

q: What is often wrong with the navigational warnings file?
a: Cancelled warnings marked as plotted, and NAVAREA, T&P, NAVTEX and EGC warnings for the passage not plotted.

q: How do you set up MSI/EGC reception on Sat-C?
a: Turn on the position feed from navigation equipment, select the message types, and switch coastal warnings on when needed (e.g. in Australia).

q: What accessories and battery rules apply to portable two-way radios?
a: Weak link, wrist and neck straps, clothing attachment. Primary battery shelf life at least 2 years, with the expiry date marked.

q: Does the company UKC policy cover the ship at anchor?
a: Inspectors asked where UKC at anchor is covered in the UKC policy, and about the policy in general.

q: What are 'confined waters' for squat calculations?
a: Depth under twice the ship's draught, or ship's beam greater than one-fifth of the waterway width.

q: What security records are checked for a piracy-area passage?
a: The security risk assessment for the passage and security rounds as per the SSP.

q: Is CPA/TCPA the same when using SOG and STW?
a: No.

q: Why use STW for collision avoidance?
a: Because the target is also using STW.

q: A small craft without AIS is on a collision course and the Master is unavailable. Will you call it on VHF?
a: The inspector wanted to hear that AIS and VHF are not to be used for collision avoidance.

q: At night, how will you get a boat's attention without VHF?
a: With light and sound signals, e.g. at least 5 short, rapid flashes and/or whistle blasts.

q: What do CATZOC 'D' and 'U' mean?
a: Survey accuracy is graded A1, A2, B, C, D and U. A1 is best and D is worst; U means unassessed, so accuracy cannot be judged.

q: Must AIS be set to low power during STS operations?
a: Not required, per section 4.14.2 of the STS guideline.

q: What VDR item should be at the VDR panel in case the Master is incapacitated?
a: A USB stick to copy the VDR data.

q: Must the engine room mode (UMS/manned) be in the passage plan?
a: Yes, for each leg at the planning stage. Not doing so was flagged.

q: Several VHFs are fitted but not all feed the VDR. What is needed?
a: Mark which units are connected and restrict use of unconnected units for critical communications.

q: How long must the GMDSS reserve source of power last?
a: Not less than 1 hr if an emergency generator is fitted, otherwise not less than 6 hrs.

q: How long do VDR recording units keep data?
a: Main DRU 48 hrs (ships built after 1 July 2014); long-term storage up to 720 hrs. DCU battery about 4 hrs.

q: What can a fixed VDR capsule withstand, and how long does its beacon transmit?
a: 1100 C and 6000 m water pressure. The beacon pings for 90 days at 37.5 kHz.

q: How does a float-free VDR capsule transmit?
a: Initially on 406 MHz, then 168 hrs on 121.5 MHz for homing.

q: How long is VDR data kept after recording stops?
a: Fixed/long-term storage 2 years; float-free capsule 6 months.

q: Why test the EPIRB within the first 5 minutes of the hour?
a: To avoid interfering with real distress signals and triggering unnecessary responses from rescue authorities.

q: What do you do after an accidental EPIRB activation?
a: Inform the RCC/MRCC as soon as possible.

q: How long does an EPIRB battery last, and how do you read its usage?
a: 48 hrs. On one maker's units the self-test flashes show use: 3 flashes 0-4 hrs, 2 flashes 5-6 hrs, 1 flash over 6 hrs.

q: When should UKC be reviewed with the pilot?
a: During the Master-pilot information exchange.

q: What is needed if electronic nautical publications are used?
a: Evidence they are flag-approved, and the required back-up publications available and maintained.

q: What is checked in the medical locker?
a: Expired medicines removed, inventory updated, O2 bottles charged and serviced, two breathing masks connected and ready.

q: Where is the procedure on ECDIS display modes?
a: Inspectors asked for the procedure on Standard, Custom and Base display modes.

q: Where is the record of EPIRB battery testing?
a: Many ships replace the EPIRB unit instead of testing the battery; be ready to show which applies.

q: What is checked in lifeboat and rescue boat stores?
a: Condition and expiry of food rations, water and pyrotechnics.

q: Where are the radar reflector and SART mounted in the survival craft?
a: Be ready to demonstrate rigging the radar reflector and the SART mounting point.

q: What do you need to know about the lifeboat air support bottles?
a: Their pressure, how it is regulated, and the final pressure at which air is released into the boat.

q: Which lifeboat equipment must be working?
a: Navigation light, searchlight, magnetic compass and internal working lights, plus the engine (tested) with fuel tank level and spare fuel inventory.

q: What else is checked on the lifeboat?
a: Pressure relief valve, steering position window glass, retro-reflective tapes, a clean propeller, and the port of registry marked on the rescue boat.

q: What launching instructions must be posted at lifeboats and liferafts?
a: Ship-specific launching procedures under emergency lighting, not generic ones.

q: How often must portable extinguishers be discharged and recharged?
a: One of each type and year of manufacture every 5 years, e.g. as part of a fire drill (IMO Res. A.951(23)). Missing records were flagged.

q: What is checked on embarkation lights?
a: They work, light the water surface well enough, and can rotate and move up/down for the lifeboat and forward liferaft.

q: What is checked on liferaft painters, HRUs and remote release wires?
a: Painters not painted, frayed or worn; HRUs fitted correctly; remote release wire of anti-twist type; embarkation ladders in good order.

q: What is checked on lifebuoys, lifejackets and immersion suits?
a: Lifelines sound and lights fixed to the buoy body; lifejacket lights working; immersion suits in good order with annual inspection done.

q: Do you need to wear a lifejacket over the immersion suit?
a: Inspectors ask this; know the answer for the suit type on board from the maker's instructions.

q: How is an immersion suit tested on board, and for how long must it hold pressure?
a: With the test kit; pressure must hold for 3 minutes.

q: What is checked on foam monitors, hydrants and hoses?
a: Monitors move freely and isolation valves are tested; hydrants do not leak; hoses are in good condition.

q: What length must fire hoses be?
a: At least 10 m, but not more than 15 m in machinery spaces, 20 m in other spaces and open decks, and 25 m on open decks of ships over 30 m breadth.

q: What is checked on breathing apparatus, EEBDs and extinguishers?
a: SCBA, fireman's outfits and IBC suits with charged bottles, EEBDs charged, extinguishers serviced, numbered and placed as per the fire plan.

q: What is checked on the SCBA compressor and fireman's radios?
a: Compressor in good condition with proper relief valves; fireman's radios fully charged at all times.

q: What foam system records are expected?
a: A foam discharge procedure using both main and emergency fire pumps, the foam analysis report and mixer pump tests.

q: Which fixed spray systems must be tested?
a: Those for the paint store, sample locker and mast riser, with records.

q: What is checked in the helicopter equipment?
a: The inventory, and that both signalling battens work.

q: Which LSA/FFA documents and records must be up to date?
a: PMS for LSA/FFA, Fire Safety Operational Booklet and SOLAS training manual (IMO symbol at their locker), CBT video records, drill and training records per planner.

q: In a SOPEP drill (spill at manifold), what detail was missing?
a: Which engine room sea chest was closed.

q: As designated distress communication officer, what must you know?
a: Be well versed in distress communication procedures.

q: What gas detection knowledge is expected from the 3/O?
a: Calibration and use of portable gas meters and the tank scope. An officer unaware of this was flagged.

q: What cargo knowledge is expected from junior officers?
a: The cargo operation, cargo hazards and the cargo plan.

q: How often must the muster list be updated?
a: It must be up to date at all times.

q: Where should the stowed lifeboat's weight be carried?
a: Not on the falls; the suspension blocks should rest on the davit horns.

q: What is needed for fire dampers?
a: A list of dampers, their maintenance, and who closes them under the emergency duties.

q: How long must the forward liferaft embarkation lamp last?
a: If it is a self-contained battery lamp, at least 3 hours.

q: What is the minimum weight of the MOB lifebuoy?
a: Not less than 4 kg.

q: Where must COSWP copies be kept?
a: On the bridge and in the crew and officers' recreation rooms. Missing copies were flagged.

q: What must be posted in the rescue boat, and what is the kill switch for?
a: The engine starting procedure. The safety pin (kill switch) stops the engine if the operator falls overboard or leaves the helm.

q: How much lifeboat fuel and air support is needed?
a: Fuel for 24 hrs at 6 kts fully loaded (know litres/hr); air for 10 minutes; able to tow a loaded liferaft at 2 kts.

q: How long must the emergency generator fuel last, and how should its start be tested?
a: Not less than 18 hours. Inspectors asked about testing it with the battery charger supply disconnected.

q: What fuel is needed for emergency engines when trading in sub-zero temperatures?
a: Fuel suited to cold: Arctic-grade diesel (pour point -40 C) is recommended. Pour point matters more than flash point; the notes say 37 C flash point is the minimum.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What sub-zero procedures are expected for deck and engine?
a: Detailed procedures for operations, equipment, heating, and fuel grades for auxiliary machinery, lifeboat engine and emergency generator.

q: What is the shelf life of diesel oil?
a: About 1-1.5 years.

q: How can the pour point of diesel be lowered with kerosene?
a: Diesel/kerosene 50/50 gives about -14 C, 40/60 about -18 C, 30/70 about -23 C.

q: What is checked on the emergency generator quick-closing valve?
a: A reset procedure must be in place.

q: What do you need to know about the steering gear reserve tank?
a: Its required capacity and how its oil level is monitored.

q: How long should a diesel emergency fire pump be able to run?
a: The notes say 3 + 15 hours.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Can emergency fire pump lines pass through the engine room?
a: They should not; if unavoidable they must be lagged.

q: Which fire detection spares are often missing from the critical spares list?
a: A smoke, a heat and a flame detector, which the list required.

q: What is your first action if the engine room floods?
a: Inspectors ask this; know the flooding contingency plan actions.

q: What is checked on self-closing sounding pipes?
a: That they work and the caps are in place and fully tight.

q: Which engine room valves need environmental seals?
a: The emergency bilge suction, bilge injection or direct suction valve.

q: What is checked on gas welding equipment?
a: Fire curtain condition, regulator in-use date, hoses free of cracks, and hose ends crimped rather than held with jubilee clips.

q: How should garbage be handled in the engine room?
a: No plastic drums; oil-soaked rags in a covered metal drum.

q: What is expected at the incinerator?
a: Operating procedure and a poster of what cannot be burnt (PCBs, cargo residues, PVC, sewage sludge, halogenated products, EGCS residues), alarm tests, sound refractory.

q: Which small sensors are commonly flagged as defective?
a: Local digital exhaust temperature sensors on auxiliary engines, and an uncalibrated IG room O2 sensor.

q: How do you get out of the engine room in a blackout?
a: Follow the IMO exit symbols along the escape route. Know where the company procedure for emergency exit is.

q: Can passwords be written near machinery control screens?
a: No.

q: What is checked on engine room floor plates and gratings?
a: That they are properly secured.

q: A running generator trips. What happens next?
a: Explain the sequence and compare how long the emergency generator and the standby generator take to come on load.

q: Where do you record a critical lube oil analysis alert?
a: In the PMS. If either of the last two LO reports shows 'Caution', an observation may be raised.

q: Why is rudder time measured 35-0-30 deg and not 35-0-35 deg?
a: The 28 s limit is from 35 deg one side to 30 deg the other; near hard over the swash plate reduces oil flow, so time increases.

q: What is checked in the Enhanced Survey Programme (ESP) file?
a: Index, ship staff inspections, executive hull summary after dry dock, incident reports for structural damage. Kept for life from 1 year before first special survey.

q: How do you calculate fuel changeover time before entering an ECA?
a: Time = number of system volumes x system volume / consumption rate. Use 3 volumes for HFO to MGO and 2 for VLSFO to ULSFO.

q: How much old fuel remains after flushing 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 system volumes?
a: 37%, 14%, 5%, 2% and under 1%. To reach 0.10% S you need under 5% old fuel, so 3 volumes.

q: What is often overlooked with fire detector test kits and the PMS?
a: The battery of the test kit, and due/overdue jobs, critical spares and work descriptions in the PMS.

q: Steering fails from the bridge, or the telegraph stops working. What then?
a: Inspectors ask for the actions; know the relevant contingency plans.

q: How long are under-piston inspection reports kept?
a: 5 years.

q: What OWS records and calibration are required?
a: A local procedure to retrieve OWS data, data kept at least 18 months, and the 15 ppm alarm calibrated every 5 years or sooner if the maker says.

q: Is the OWS tested before port arrival?
a: The company in the notes required a test 24 hrs before arrival, logged in ORB Part I.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: How is a deck crane slewing bearing checked?
a: By a rocking test or analysis of the gear grease; know the alternative method.

q: What do inspectors expect about SIMOPS?
a: A procedure identifying potential SIMOPS, a decision matrix and controls. Officers and ratings must know the term and their duties.

q: What entry procedure applies to spaces like the emergency fire pump room or bilge-level test spaces?
a: A defined entry procedure; inspectors asked to see it.

q: What must the N2/IG room entry procedure record?
a: The atmosphere check results and entry/exit times, in line with the SMS. An officer unaware of the form was flagged.

q: Which gases are checked during bunkering, and who checks them?
a: Know the gases and who tests them. The C/O's daily gas check should go to the engine room and be logged.

q: How do you enter the engine room during UMS?
a: Call the bridge and switch on the dead-man alarm before entry.

q: Is a dead-man alarm a statutory requirement? What about the engineers' call?
a: Dead-man alarm: no. Engineers' call alarm: yes.

q: What do AS1, AS2 and AS3 mean in the bunkering checklist?
a: Agreement Sheet (1, 2 and 3).

q: How many threads should protrude on bunker manifold bolts?
a: At least 1.5 threads beyond the nut. Undersized bolts were flagged.

q: What must not be stored in the acetylene compartment?
a: Combustible material.

q: An auxiliary engine insulation cover is bent and reads 300 C. Why is it a finding?
a: Damaged insulation exposes hot surfaces; check exhaust pipes for any visible hot surface.

q: What should the C/E's standing orders cover?
a: Aligned with the Master's orders: alarm and defect actions, oil transfers, incinerator use, workshop work, UMS rounds and entry, dead-man alarm, and when to call the C/E.

q: Must the C/E's engine orders be timed?
a: Yes. Orders and the EOW's reading of them should be timed.

q: Where is the record of sea water pipeline inspection?
a: Inspectors asked to see it.

q: What are HP and LP SCR?
a: Selective catalytic reduction for Tier III NOx compliance: HP is fitted before the turbocharger, LP after it.

q: How are bunker samples taken and disposed of?
a: Know the sampling method during bunkering and how retained samples are disposed of (ashore or to a bunker tank).

q: Do you have a risk assessment for managing AMS alarms?
a: Inspectors asked for one.

q: If a machinery alarm is not acknowledged, when must the engineers' alarm sound?
a: Within 5 minutes. A new alarm while the first is still active must also be announced.

q: How often is emergency lighting tested?
a: Weekly, per the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: What voltage rating must rubber mats at the MSB/ESB have?
a: At least 10,000 V, shown on the back of the mat or by a certificate.

q: There is only one hose handling crane. What is needed?
a: A risk assessment to decide the critical spares for that crane.

q: What engine room watch details must be logged?
a: Watch levels for each operation, the C/E taking over control, and the names of oilers on watch.

q: The company leaves the highest engine watch level to the C/E. How do you decide?
a: Inspectors ask how the C/E decides to put that level in force; know your criteria.

q: What is expected after structural repairs?
a: They must be in the defect reporting system with an incident report where needed. Know the superintendent's response time.

q: How should acids and alkalis be stored?
a: Physically separated. Storing them together was flagged and missed in the safety inspection.

q: Where is the procedure for setting the insulation monitoring (earth fault) alarm?
a: Inspectors asked for it in the company manual.

q: What is SEEMP and how do you meet it?
a: Explain the ship energy efficiency management plan (from 1 Jan 2013) and the package of measures on board to improve efficiency.

q: What output voltage is allowed for a welding machine?
a: Not more than 25 V AC or 70 V DC (COSWP 24.6), with a local switch to cut current to the electrode quickly.

q: Which N2 generator alarms should be tested?
a: Electric heater failure, low feed-air pressure/flow, high air temperature, and high condensate level at the water separator drain.

q: What is expected for the local water-mist (hypermist) system?
a: Quarterly water quality checks, auto mode during UMS, low-level alarm or marked minimum level, and cover arranged while its tank is cleaned.

q: What is needed around transformers?
a: An electric shock treatment notice and rubber mats.

q: How will you pump out a flooded steering gear room?
a: Inspectors ask this; know the arrangement on board.

q: The ship ran in manned mode on open sea passages due to reliability concerns. What was missing?
a: A defect report for the cause of the concern.

q: Which IG system valves need an O&M procedure?
a: Boiler uptake valve, gas regulating valve, scrubber valve and demister valve.

q: Does the emergency generator need a NOx technical file?
a: Not mandatory. Where a NOx file exists, part numbers must match the maker's manual.

q: What procedure is needed for the emergency compressor?
a: Operation and testing of the emergency compressor and air reservoir.

q: Can the ship run UMS with SOLAS II-1 Part E equipment defective?
a: No. Operating UMS with such equipment out of service was flagged.

q: What notice is required for a CPP?
a: A notice on the bridge or in the machinery space showing the CPP failure mode.

q: What spares should be in the emergency generator room?
a: A spare starter motor and critical spares for the emergency generator.

q: How is the emergency battery system tested?
a: Periodically as a complete system, brought on load as part of a blackout simulation.

q: What is expected for an EGCS (scrubber)?
a: Crew training on its operation and calibration, plus the SOx compliance plan, technical manual, monitoring manual and EGCS record book.

q: What fire-prevention checklist is needed for machinery spaces?
a: A ship-specific checklist covering hot surfaces and flammable liquids.

q: Which engines need an oil mist detector, and what alarm setting is expected?
a: Engines of 2250 kW+ or bore over 300 mm. A set point above 5% LEL (about 2.5 mg/l) was flagged.

q: Where must large hydraulic power packs be installed?
a: Packs over 50 kW and 100 bar: dedicated space with separate ventilation. In the main ER they need oil mist detection or encapsulation with leak detection.

q: What is EPL, and how is it set?
a: Inspectors asked engineers to explain engine power limitation, its setting and ShaPoLi.

q: Which small engine room findings are common?
a: Oil-soaked nylon slings and loose mist catcher vanes on ER blowers.

q: Is the cargo oil pump bulkhead seal in the PMS?
a: It should be; inspectors asked to see it.

q: What VOC management knowledge is checked in the CCR?
a: The target tank pressure in the approved VOC plan, procedures to minimise VOC emissions, and crew training on the VOC plan.

q: What happens to cargo operations if the IG system fails?
a: Know the actions on IG failure and whether crude or products may be discharged, as set out in the company procedure.

q: What information about loading and venting capacity must be posted?
a: Inspectors check that the loading rate and venting capacity information is posted.

q: What are the company requirements for testing cargo tank high-level alarms?
a: Know the required tests and their frequency.

q: What is pyrophoric oxidation?
a: Spontaneous ignition of certain materials when exposed to air, caused by rapid oxidation that releases enough heat to ignite without an external source.

q: How many emergency stop buttons are on board, and where?
a: Know the number and locations of all emergency stops.

q: How often are ship/shore safety repeat checks made?
a: Show the written procedure and evidence that repeat checks were done at the required intervals.

q: Where are the instructions on which vents are open or closed in port?
a: Know where the procedure is.

q: What is the pump room entry procedure?
a: Inspectors ask CCR staff to explain it.

q: What PPE should the deck watchkeeper wear during cargo operations?
a: At least chemical goggles and gloves, standing clear of the hoses, with a full set of chemical PPE ready near the manifold.

q: Does your ECDIS have IHO S-52 Presentation Library 4.0, and how can you show it?
a: Inspectors expect you to show on screen which Presentation Library version is loaded.

q: What is the README.TXT file, and what does it tell you?
a: A file from the chart service that announces changes such as the new symbols in Presentation Library 4.0.

q: What are the IHO test ENCs supplied with an ECDIS called?
a: ECDIS Chart 1.

q: What is the difference between the ECDIS type approval certificate and the declaration of conformity?
a: The type approval certificate is issued by a third party (class); the DoC by the maker. The installation date must fall between issue and expiry dates.

q: True or false: a manual update applies to one selected ENC, not to a whole geographical area like a user chart.
a: True.

q: What is UKHO's next-generation ENC called?
a: High Density ENC.

q: How long a power interruption must the main ECDIS survive without manual re-initialisation?
a: 45 seconds.

q: What is the CCPR feature of ECDIS?
a: Collision Course and Point of Risk.

q: What is CCRP on ECDIS?
a: Consistent common reference point. When it is switched on, the common reference point jumps forward.

q: What is the standard size of the isolated danger symbol on ECDIS?
a: 7 mm, so it stays visible at all scales.

q: True or false: ENCs with producer code IN (India) include T&P corrections in their weekly updates.
a: True, per the T&P status file issued in February 2024.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: True or false: Taiwan ENCs (1U) showing a 'Non-Official ENC' warning may still be used for navigation.
a: True, per the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: If no safety contour is set, what does ECDIS default to?
a: 30 metres, per the IMO performance standards.

q: A dual-ECDIS ship shuts down the back-up ECDIS for a few days mid-ocean. Is that a violation?
a: Yes.

q: How often do you verify the ECDIS sensors?
a: Every watch.

q: How do you cross-check GPS position accuracy on ECDIS?
a: With the radar overlay.

q: What is the ADMIRALTY Information Overlay (AIO)?
a: A weekly-updated worldwide dataset shown over ENCs. It flags navigationally significant differences UKHO cartographers find between ENCs and paper charts.

q: How does the GPS work out magnetic variation?
a: From latitude, longitude, altitude, date and the World Magnetic Model, which BGS and NGDC update every 5 years.

q: Should you set a trigger alarm when you make a manual update or user chart entry?
a: Yes.

q: What is safety information promulgated by a local authority for ENCs called?
a: MSI, handled like a T&P notice.

q: What are EP NMs, and what do they show?
a: ENC Preliminary Notices to Mariners. They highlight navigationally significant differences between ENCs and ADMIRALTY paper charts.

q: What is the AIO 'No Overlay' polygon?
a: A shaded block where no equivalent-scale paper chart exists, so UKHO cannot compare coverage or add information.

q: What is the date-dependent view used for?
a: Seasonal or time-limited information pops up when a feature is selected. Keep date-dependent view on.

q: What does a 'd' symbol on the ECDIS mean?
a: The ENC producer has coded the feature with time-based attributes such as a start or end date.

q: What is the SA certificate?
a: The Scheme Administrator certificate - an electronic key from the service provider. Be ready to show your permit file and what it contains.

q: What is the difference between cancellation and withdrawal of an ENC?
a: A cancelled ENC is replaced by a reissue; a withdrawn ENC is removed completely. Record it in the ENC log (the notes cite NP133C).

q: What does a Security Scheme Error SSE 25 alert mean?
a: The ENC is no longer valid for use.

q: What is NP231?
a: The ADMIRALTY Guide to the Practical Use of ENCs.

q: Should T&Ps on ECDIS be marked whether they came as an ENC update or a new edition?
a: Yes.

q: How do you know which ENCs contain T&P notices and which countries do not include them?
a: Check the ADMIRALTY AVCS information on admiralty.co.uk/avcs. Missing T&Ps must be plotted on the ENC yourself.

q: What is the latest version of the AIO user guide?
a: October 2023, per the notes.
t: Check against the current regulation / your company procedure.

q: Can you use AIO to receive T&Ps for paper charts?
a: No.

q: What is compilation scale, and where can you find it?
a: The scale at which the ENC data was compiled. Zooming in or out loads or sheds layers of information. The pick report shows the compilation scale.

q: Why is chart scale important on ECDIS?
a: Inspectors ask why the appropriate scale matters and the difference between the largest scale chart and the largest appropriate chart.

q: Which safety contour is being displayed right now?
a: Be ready to point out on screen the contour the ECDIS is using as the safety contour.

q: Why are some soundings highlighted and others not?
a: Soundings shallower than the set depth limit are highlighted; deeper ones are not. Know how safety depth differs from safety contour.
t: The notes call the limit 'shallow depth'. Check against your ECDIS settings.

q: What is the look-ahead (safety frame) used for, and how is it set?
a: Situational awareness. Set time and distance, and know which values to use at sea, in port approaches and approaching an anchorage.

q: How often do you update both ECDIS units?
a: As set by company policy.

q: What is area symbolisation, and why keep it on?
a: It makes areas (e.g. restricted areas) apparent with symbols.

q: What is the S-100 standard?
